question: Can the original 14-run fit predict the peak ISS optical response in other SAME-R runs under the same four nominal settings?
selection_timing: The team fixed this analysis plan and the predictions from runs 73–86 before extracting the comparison workbooks for this follow-up. This retrospective check has no independent timestamp.
training: Exactly the published 14 base runs numbered 73 through 86, inclusive. Fit the heater-only ordinary least-squares model once. Clamp negative predictions to zero.
comparators: Mean peak drop across all training runs
Median peak drop across all training runs
Mean peak drop among training runs of the named material
cohort: All other numeric base IDs in the v4 condition table matching these four fields. Require one unambiguous material and an analyzed reduced-gravity workbook with matching folder material and run identifier. Exclude aged suffixes. Record all unmatched or unscorable settings.

primary_exclusions.90: This condition lists a reburn of training run 85.
primary_exclusions.92: The earlier FIRST FIRE detector power case already inspected the optical trace.
primary_exclusions.93: The earlier FIRST FIRE detector power case already inspected the optical trace.

target: Median native ISS scatter voltage over the 30 s preceding heater onset minus minimum native ISS scatter voltage from onset through 300 s, inclusive. Require finite readings, self-test off, coverage to within 1 s of both ends and no gap exceeding 2 s. Use the first minimum in a tie.
metrics: Run-weighted mean absolute error in volts is primary. Report errors by material, earlier/later run number relative to training, equal-material mean, and all usable runs including the three overlap checks. Do not use alarm flags, the published 2 V line or a selected voltage range as an endpoint.
scope: Same PSI study, instrument and five training materials. Material labels and prescribed heater settings are available before optical response. No inference about unseen materials, mission-independent replication, concentration, particle detection rate or cabin alarms.
